recent_posts.title: Practical Codex automations for iOS developers
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of practical AI agent automations for iOS developers using OpenAI's Codex app. Covers five automation ideas: nightly issue triage, keeping architectural documentation in sync with code, test suite health monitoring (leveraging Xcode's new MCP integration), product discoverability audits, and a daily single-improvement suggestion. Each automation includes a sample prompt and tips for refinement. The core argument is that low-stakes background automations are the ideal entry point for experimenting with AI coding agents before trusting them with larger tasks.

recent_posts.title: How to find SF symbol names directly in Xcode without the SF Symbols app
recent_posts.summary: SF Symbols can be browsed and searched directly inside Xcode without switching to the dedicated SF Symbols app. In Xcode, go to View > Show Library and open the fourth tab to access a searchable list of all SF symbol names. The standalone SF Symbols app still has value for previewing animations and color variants, but for simply finding a symbol name, Xcode's built-in library is sufficient.

recent_posts.title: How to use a Raw Identifier as a function name
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.0 introduces raw identifiers for function names, enabling developers to use test descriptions directly as function names in Swift Testing. This eliminates the need for abbreviated function names and allows special characters, whitespace, leading digits, and operators in identifiers, streamlining the test-writing experience.

recent_posts.title: Using an Optional in a String interpolation
recent_posts.summary: Swift 6.2 introduces improved syntax for handling optionals in string interpolation. Instead of using the nil coalescing operator, developers can now specify default values directly within the interpolation. This new approach is more flexible, allowing the default value's type to differ from the optional's type, which resolves compilation errors that the nil coalescing operator couldn't handle.

How to disable Liquid Glass in your iOS app (iOS 26 tutorial)
recent_posts.summary: iOS 26 introduces a new Liquid Glass design system that may break existing apps. Developers can temporarily opt out by adding the 'UI design requires compatibility' key set to 'yes' in their app's info.plist file. This compatibility option will be deprecated with iOS 27, so developers should plan to properly support Liquid Glass soon.

recent_posts.title: How to hide the content of a view in a screenshot (iOS tutorial)
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to hide view content during iOS screenshots using an unofficial workaround. The technique leverages UITextField's secure text entry behavior by extracting its screenshot-hiding subview and applying it to any arbitrary view. While functional, this method is hacky and not guaranteed to work in future iOS versions.

recent_posts.title: Xcode 16 AI features review and comparison with alternatives
recent_posts.summary: Xcode 16's new AI features have significant limitations compared to competitors like Cursor. Key shortcomings include no request queuing, lack of context/rules configuration, no build validation, missing Git integration, no terminal access, and limited project file scope. While these features provide a good introduction to AI-assisted coding for newcomers, developers seeking daily AI usage should consider more powerful alternatives like Cursor or Claude Code due to Xcode's current constraints.

recent_posts.title: TaskGroup results ordering pitfall and solution
recent_posts.summary: TaskGroup results are collected in completion order, not creation order, which can lead to unexpected random ordering. To maintain the original task creation order, modify tasks to return tuples containing both the input parameter and result, then sort the collected results using this additional information.

recent_posts.title: How to access Xcode 26's hidden ChatGPT system prompt
recent_posts.summary: Xcode 26's ChatGPT integration includes a hidden system prompt that provides context and guidelines to improve AI responses. The prompt instructs the AI to act as a coding assistant, prioritize Swift and Apple frameworks, use Swift concurrency over older patterns, and provides specific formatting rules for code suggestions. Developers can access this hidden prompt by using network monitoring tools like Proximan to intercept API calls to OpenAI, revealing valuable insights about how the AI integration works and how to better interact with it.
